results.correct_value: loss_ft 9700 (equal to gain_ft; the route returns to the Diablo trailhead)
results.evidence: The stored 1,788 ft is a different quantity: it is the drop from Stetattle Ridge's north peak to the base of Elephant Butte, stated as exactly 1,788 ft on a Stetattle Ridge/Sourdough page. A two-day ascent account from Diablo gives nearly 10,000 ft of gain and loss over roughly 20 miles, and another account from the ridge high point describes 2,500+ ft of gain and descent each way beyond the ridge before repeating it on the return. The route is out-and-back to the same trailhead, so total loss equals total gain (9,700 ft).

results.fact: Total trip time vs its own approach/summit/descent legs
results.evidence: The 36-hour total reads as elapsed time for a two-day trip, while the three leg times (5/3/4 h) add to 12. One account puts the summit day from a Stetattle Ridge camp at about 10 hours of travel (so the 3-hour summit leg looks low); a fast single-push party estimated the whole trip at about 16 hours. No two sources give agreeing leg times or a car-to-car total, so nothing was changed.

results.correct_value: Exit from Whatcom Pass down Brush Creek, across the Chilliwack and over Hannegan Pass to the Hannegan trailhead
results.evidence: Whatcom Pass connects to the Brush Creek/Chilliwack trail (Hannegan side) and to Little Beaver Creek, not to the Big Beaver Trail; Big Beaver serves Wiley Ridge and Access Creek. A trip to the Crooked Thumb Glacier moraine camp (Ghost's immediate neighbours) went in and out via the Hannegan trailhead, the Chilliwack cable car, Brush Creek and Whatcom Pass. The row's own six-day itinerary (Hannegan in and out) agrees; only this sentence named Big Beaver/Ross Lake.

results.evidence: Hannegan trailhead to Whatcom Pass is about 16-17 mi one way (a mapped route gives 16.0 mi; a trip report gives 17), matching both the waypoint (16) and itinerary days 1-2 (16.2). results.correct_value: rope_note should not claim that no route-specific account exists
results.evidence: The first-ascent account of the 1970 Carpetbaggers Traverse describes this exact line (notch south of the peak, gained from the west, south and west sides, easy to moderate fifth-class pitches), and an encyclopedia entry independently records the 1970 Firey/Firey/Knudson/Renz ascent and a Class 4 west-face route. The claim that no route-specific account exists is false; the rest of the rope advice is kept.

results.fact: high camp location: Crooked Thumb Glacier moraine vs Luna Cirque/Lousy Lake
results.evidence: The approach and itinerary put the high camp on the Crooked Thumb Glacier moraine, while the waypoint 'Luna Cirque high camp (near Lousy Lake)' and descent_text ('Luna Cirque camp at Luna or Lousy Lake') put it in Luna Cirque; Lousy Lake lies at the base of Luna Cirque. The first-ascent line gained the notch from the west, and a Hannegan-side party camped on the Crooked Thumb Glacier moraine for the neighbouring peaks, but no second source names Ghost's camp, so nothing was changed.

results.fact: Ross Lake described as serving only Luna/Fury
results.evidence: The approach, the Hannegan Pass waypoint's directions and the itinerary/sectionBreakdown notes say Ross Lake serves only Luna/Fury, but Ross Lake also reaches Whatcom Pass via Little Beaver Creek (about 18 trail miles) and the Challenger Glacier via Big Beaver and Wiley Ridge, as the row's own Beaver Pass bivy entry says. Hannegan remains a standard approach; the framing is overstated, but rewriting it touches several fields and is left for review.

results.correct_value: About 16 mi one way to the summit, about 32 mi round trip
results.evidence: A mapped route puts Whatcom Pass 16.0 mi from the Hannegan trailhead, and trail mileages give the Brush Creek junction-to-Whatcom Pass leg as 5.1 mi one way; Indian Mountain is climbed from the Brush Creek trail below Whatcom Pass, so the summit lies about 16 mi in, not 18-20. The row's waypoints (leave trail at 14.5, summit at 16) and itinerary (14+4+14 = 32 mi) agree.
